data.item: • QUARTERLY GDP GROWTH – GDP growth is projected to decelerate this year, as higher inflationary pressures, unpredictable weather patterns and tighter monetary policy slows down demand. • USD/KES – There has been high demand for dollars in the market with reduced supply pushing the prices up. • The demand pressure is likely to push the local currency further into the year.

• Interbank Rates – The money market remained liquid during the quarter ending 30th June partly reflecting government payments, which offset tax remittances. • T-Bill Rates – There has been an upward move within the curve i.e. 91-day, 182-day and 364-day treasury bills. The longer end of the curve has also been affected and has seen investors seeking higher rates.
